title: Is belief in God rational—and who was Jesus?
claim_under_test: The evidence does not force either atheism or theism, but belief in God is rationally defensible; Jesus of Nazareth is historically real and his ultimate identity remains a disputed interpretive question.

current_assessment.summary: God has not been scientifically disproved or mathematically proven. Philosophical arguments and historical claims are cumulative. Jesus was a first-century Jewish teacher crucified under Pontius Pilate; claims about his resurrection and divine identity are interpretation-dependent.
current_assessment.certainty_note: Strong on the limits of categorical proof and on Jesus' historical existence/crucifixion; disputed on metaphysics and resurrection.

strongest_counterargument: Naturalistic explanations, suffering, divine hiddenness, and religious diversity may explain the evidence without positing God.
what_would_change_the_finding: demonstration that the arguments are logically invalid and naturalistic alternatives explain all cited data better
decisive correction to the historical claims about Jesus
new evidence materially bearing on the resurrection traditions

revision_history.change: Case opened with first-pass deep-dive investigation.
